item.title: Hostels warn €8 tourist tax could wipe out Maltas backpacker market
item.description: A group of nine licensed hostels have warned that the increased eco-contribution could wipe out Maltas backpacker niche market and threaten the survival of independent operators. They called for a tiered system based on accommodation category, saying the flat €8 fee could force several hostels to close their doors. They said they are not asking for visitors to be exempt from contributing to Maltas environmental and tourism sustainability objectives but for a fairer and more proportionate approach, noting that most European destinations charge lower rates for budget accommodation.

item.title: Government to publish document on tenants rights and obligations
item.description: The government will prepare a document setting out the rights and obligations of those entering a rental contract, complementing the Buyers Charter. The initiative follows a public consultation on the Buyers Charter that drew 33 submissions, with feedback that people living in rented property also need clarity on their rights and responsibilities. Accommodation and Arts Minister Owen Bonnici made the announcement at a meeting with property-sector professionals organised by the Housing Authority, saying both initiatives are part of government work to improve transparency, certainty and trust in the sector.

item.title: Traditional Maltese mazzit joins ġbejna on EU protected foods list
item.description: The European Commission has approved the registration of traditional Maltese blood pudding mazzit as a Protected Geographical Indication in a regulation published on Friday. The listing places mazzit in the EUs eAmbrosia register of geographical indications, joining thousands of protected European products, with only producers meeting specific requirements able to use the protected name. The recognition follows a years-long effort led by the Public Abattoir to revive a product authorities say was at risk of disappearing, and comes less than two years after ġbejna received EU protection.

item.title: Court rules deportation of father of two young children disproportionate
item.description: A court has ruled that the deportation of a father of two young children was disproportionate because immigration authorities failed to consider the impact on his family. Balwinder Singh, 39, was convicted in August of presenting forged architect documents falsely stating that five people could live in a property instead of three, and received a four-month suspended sentence. A principal immigration officer then issued the deportation order; Singh challenged it before the Immigration Appeals Board while in detention, and the board upheld his appeal and ordered his release.

item.title: Widow sues care home over husbands death after alleged assault by resident
item.description: A widow has filed a civil lawsuit against the operators of a Fgura care home after her husband died following an alleged assault by his roommate. Antonia Perini is seeking damages over the death of Giuseppe Perini, who was attacked at Dar San Ġużepp on 14 October 2025 and died at Mater Dei Hospital two weeks later after suffering serious injuries. She claims the attack was carried out by a fellow resident in the same room who allegedly had a history of behavioural problems associated with severe dementia.

item.title: Animal care clinic to get €700,000 more next year, reaching €1.35 million
item.description: Funding for the animal care clinic will increase by €700,000 next year, taking its total allocation to €1.35 million under Budget 2027. Parliamentary Secretary for Animal Welfare Alicia Bugeja Said said three support schemes for voluntary organisations and sanctuaries will also be relaunched: the Free Veterinary Services Scheme, the Maintenance of Animal Sanctuaries Scheme and the Animal Welfare Fund. She said the additional funding would strengthen animal care services and support organisations that dedicate themselves to the work.

item.title: Over 6,000 people helped by Victim Support Agency in five years
item.description: More than 6,000 people have received assistance from the Victim Support Agency since it was established five years ago. The agencys panic alarm service was used by 125 people in the first ten months of this year, against 84 across the whole of 2025. Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said a common referral system would be strengthened so that victims are directed to the services they need without having to repeatedly recount their traumatic experiences, linking victim protection directly to crime prevention.

item.title: Gozo-Sicily agreement aims to open new markets for Gozitan producers
item.description: Gozo and Sicily have signed a memorandum of understanding expected to create new opportunities for Gozitan farmers, fishermen and businesses. The agreement, signed between CNA Sicilia and the Gozo Confederation for Agriculture and Fisheries during the Taormina Food Expo, will facilitate exports, the promotion of Gozitan products and collaboration between businesses on the two islands. Gozo Minister Clint Camilleri said it could lead to joint Mediterranean brands capable of competing in international markets.

item.title: Medservs nine-month EBITDA climbs 8.5% to €17.8 million
item.description: MedservRegis published an interim report showing revenue up 30% to €89.1 million for the first nine months of 2026, with EBITDA advancing 8.5% to €17.8 million. The company said it expects full-year 2026 results to remain ahead of the forecasts in its updated Financial Analysis Summary dated 19 June 2026, which projected revenue of €99.8 million and EBITDA of €21.9 million. The results were published after the close of trading, in a session when the MSE Equity Price Index edged up 0.26% to 4,307.3 points.

item.title: Scientists discover 200m seabed bulge linked to fault system shaping Malta and Gozo
item.description: Scientists have identified a massive underwater bulge rising 200m above the surrounding seabed between Malta and the Italian island of Pantelleria. The structure stretches 26km in length and 4.6km in width at depths between 1,400m and 1,750m in the northern sector of the Malta Graben, lying 60km to 80km west-northwest of Malta. The findings were published in the journal Tectonophysics in a study led by Nicolò Chizzini of Italys National Institute of Geophysics and Volcanology.

item.title: MPT investigates clash between passenger and bus inspector caught on camera
item.description: Malta Public Transport is investigating an altercation between a bus inspector and a passenger caught on camera on Friday morning. Footage shared on social media shows the passenger pushing the inspector on the Route 82B bus towards Birżebbuġa, with the inspector then grabbing the passenger by the neck, while another passenger is heard asking whether he can buy the man a €2 ticket. The dispute appears to have arisen over an unpaid bus ticket; the company said it has zero tolerance for violence.

item.title: Marc Alden to step down as Deloitte Malta CEO in June 2027
item.description: Marc Alden will step down as chief executive of Deloitte Malta in June 2027, closing a leadership tenure spanning two terms. Alden joined the firm in 1994 and has led it as CEO since January 2020, meaning that by then he will have served the maximum two terms permitted under the firms governance rules. He will remain with Deloitte Malta as a partner taking on the role of Government and Public Sector Business Leader, and said he looked forward to working more closely with government as Malta enters an important period of transformation.

item.title: Winners of Maltas oldest architectural and conservation awards announced
item.description: A converted guesthouse in Senglea with a contemporary rooftop extension was the overall winner of the 20th edition of the Din l-Art Ħelwa Architectural Heritage Awards. Stilla San Mikiel, the second property in an albergo diffuso spread across the Three Cities, was designed by Valentino Architects and received the Judge Maurice Caruana Curran Award, also sharing the Rehabilitation and Re-use of Buildings Award with Elementi, a wellness and hospitality project in Mosta. A public garden in the former oil storage depot in Birgu was among the other winners.
